The Essential Motorcycle Touring Toolkit

You do not need a full workshop on tour. These 12 items cover 95% of roadside issues and weigh under 2kg total. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Read our The Ultimate Motorcycle Touring Packing List guide for more. Read our Essential Motorcycle Toolkit for Long-Distance Touring guide for more.

  1. Multi-tool — Quick adjustments
  2. Tyre Repair Kit — Plug punctures in minutes
  3. Mini Air Pump — Restore tyre pressure
  4. Tyre Pressure Gauge — Check pressures daily
  5. Spare Fuses — Electrical failures sorted
  6. Cable Ties — The duct tape of motorcycling
  7. Duct Tape — Temporary fix for almost anything
  8. Chain Lube — Keep drivetrain smooth
  9. Torch/Headlamp — Night-time repairs
  10. Spare Bulbs — MOT-legal lighting
  11. Allen Key Set — Hex bolts on most bikes
  12. Adjustable Spanner — Universal bolt turning
Pro Tip: Practice using each tool at home before you need it roadside.
keyTakeaways: Twelve carefully chosen tools cover around 95% of roadside issues and weigh under 2kg.
A tyre repair kit and mini air pump let you plug punctures and restore pressure roadside.
Cable ties and duct tape provide quick temporary fixes for a huge range of problems.
Spare fuses and bulbs keep your electrics and MOT-legal lighting working.
Practise using each tool at home before you need it at the roadside.

faq.q: What tools should I carry on a motorcycle tour?
faq.a: A practical kit covers a tyre repair kit, a mini air pump, a pressure gauge, a multi-tool, spare fuses and bulbs, cable ties, duct tape, chain lube, a torch, an Allen key set and a small adjustable spanner. These twelve items handle the vast majority of roadside problems and weigh under 2kg in total.

faq.q: How heavy should a touring toolkit be?
faq.a: You do not need a full workshop on the bike. A focused kit of the twelve essentials weighs under 2kg and fits in a small pouch or under the seat. The aim is to fix or bodge enough to reach the next town or a garage, not to carry out major repairs at the roadside.

faq.q: Can I really fix a puncture with a repair kit?
faq.a: For tubeless tyres, a plug-style repair kit lets you seal most punctures in minutes, and a mini pump or CO2 inflator restores pressure enough to ride to a garage. It is a temporary fix, so have the tyre inspected or replaced afterwards. Practise the technique at home so you are not learning it in the rain.

faq.q: Why carry cable ties and duct tape?
faq.a: Cable ties and duct tape are the motorcyclist's best friends for improvised repairs. They can hold a cracked fairing or dangling bodywork in place, secure a loose cable, or bundle a broken part until you reach help. They weigh almost nothing and get you out of trouble more often than any single spanner.

faq.q: Should I practise using my tools before a trip?
faq.a: Absolutely. Learning how to plug a tyre, change a bulb or adjust your chain in a warm, dry garage is far easier than doing it for the first time at the roadside in poor conditions. Run through each tool at home so you know it fits your bike and you can use it confidently when it matters.
